Offline update packages

Update a node with no route to the code repository — a signed package with the application and the Python wheels it may be missing, verified against a root-owned trust store and applied by the privileged runner with automatic rollback.

👤 ForAdministratorAdvanced user
🔑 Permissionsusers.manage
📍 WhereSoftware Update page (URL /self-update), card "Offline update package"; CLI satom execute update package / fetch

Overview#

An offline update package updates SATOM on a node that cannot reach the code repository: no Internet, no git remote, no package mirror. It is not the offline install bundle — it carries only the application and its pinned Python wheels, not operating-system packages.

satom-update-<version>/
    manifest.json   the signed document: version, sha256 of every file, python_tags, min_from_version
    manifest.sig    Ed25519 signature over the exact bytes of manifest.json
    app.tar.gz      the application tree at that revision
    wheels/*.whl    the pinned Python dependencies a node may be missing

⚠️Warning — Coming from 3.3.2 or older

From 3.3.4 a package ships only the wheels 3.3.3 does not already have, and it accepts only a node on 3.3.3 or newer. On an older node it stops at Upgrade path without changing anything. Apply satom-update-3.3.3.tar.gz (release v3.3.3, which carries every wheel) first, then the newer package.

Every node refuses an unsigned package. Releases publish the package, its .sha256 and the public key it is signed with, so you normally do not build one yourself.

Who can do it#

Where Requirement
Software Update page (/self-update) — upload, preflight, apply, check the feed users.manage (the routes check the coarse user_manage key); without it the routes return 403
satom execute update package / update fetch root on the node (sudo satom …)

Getting a package onto the node#

Method How
Upload Software Update → Offline update package → choose satom-update-<version>.tar.gz → Upload & check
Release feed (node with HTTPS access) Check for a newer package online → Download & stage (runs as a background job), or sudo satom execute update fetch --download-only
CLI, file already on the node sudo satom execute update package satom-update-<version>.tar.gz --yes
  • Uploads are limited to 400 MB and must be named like satom-update-1.3.6.tar.gz (letters, digits, ., _, -).
  • The feed is only read when someone asks; nothing polls. A download whose size or sha256 does not match the feed is deleted; a match still has to pass the signature check. Point a node at a mirror with SATOM_UPGRADE_FEED or --feed <https-url>.

❗Important — In a pair, stage on the primary

data/ (including the staging area data/update-uploads/) is copied from the primary to the standby with rsync --delete. A package uploaded on the standby disappears at the next sync. Each node applies its own copy (each has its own virtual environment): standby first, then the primary.

Preflight#

After upload the page shows a preflight report. Nothing is applied yet.

Check Blocks apply Catches
Trust store yes no trusted keys, or a store that is not root-owned
Archive yes path traversal, symlinks, device nodes
Signature & integrity yes unsigned, unknown key, altered or extra files
Version no (warning) downgrade, or the same version again
Upgrade path yes the package needs a newer starting version (min_from_version)
Python yes the node's venv does not match the package's wheels
Dependencies yes a changed pin with no wheel in the package
Disk space yes less free space than about 3 × the package size
This node no (warning) staging on a standby

The checks are advisory: when you press Apply package to this node the server re-runs the preflight, and the privileged runner verifies the signature, hashes and version rules again as root.

Applying#

  1. 1Apply package to this nodepreflight re-run; request written to data/update-requests/
  2. 2satom-updater.pathstarts the root runner (satom-updater.service)
  3. 3Verifyrunner not writable by the service account; signature; every hash; version rules
  4. 4Database backuptaken first; the apply refuses to continue without it
  5. 5Freeze dependenciesso the venv can be restored
  6. 6Installpark local commits, install the tree, pip install --no-index from the package wheels
  7. 7Migrate and refreshflask db upgrade (fatal on failure), units, CLI, the runner itself
  8. 8Restart and check/healthz must answer 200
  9. 9Committhe deployed revision is recorded

The page shows the live status of each step. The web service restarts during the update.

On any failure the runner resets the tree to the previous commit, removes only the files the package added, restores the virtual environment from the freeze, restarts the services and checks health again.

⚠️Warning — Database changes are not rolled back

If a migration fails part-way, the code and libraries are rolled back but the database is not. Restore the backup the apply took before retrying: satom get backup list, then sudo satom execute restore db <bundle> --yes.

Downgrades#

Allowed, but migrations are never reversed. In the console tick "I understand this is a downgrade…"; with the CLI pass --allow-downgrade. Without the confirmation the console answers "This package is OLDER than the running version. Tick the downgrade confirmation to proceed — migrations are not reversed, so keep the database backup."

Trust store#

The public keys a node accepts live in /etc/satom/update-keys/, owned by root:root together with every parent directory, outside the application tree (so the web process cannot add its own key). The installer trusts the release keys shipped in deploy/update-keys/. A node with an empty trust store accepts nothing.

satom show trust                                   # keys this node accepts
sudo satom execute trust add-key release.pub       # compare the fingerprint first
sudo satom execute trust remove-key <name|fingerprint> --yes
satom diagnose updates                             # is the whole path sound?

ℹ️Note — One key, one use (3.0)

This trust store verifies update packages (and legacy 2.x API packs) only. 3.0 API and knowledge packs are verified with the keys of their own lane, shipped with the release, and trust add-key --purpose api_pack|knowledge adds one under /etc/satom/pack-keys/<lane>/. The update verifier never reads a pack key. See Pack trust.

Each node has its own trust store; add keys on both nodes of a pair. To rotate a key: install the new public key everywhere, sign the next release with it, then remove the old one.

Building and signing your own package#

# build — any machine with a checkout; holds no secret
bash installers/build-update-package.sh            # → dist/satom-update-<version>.tar.gz

# create a signing key once (encrypted private key; back it up offline)
python3 deploy/sign_update_package.py genkey --out release --comment "<owner>"

# sign — where the private key lives, never on a managed node
python3 deploy/sign_update_package.py sign dist/satom-update-<version>.tar.gz --key release.key
python3 deploy/sign_update_package.py verify dist/satom-update-<version>.tar.gz --pub release.pub
Builder variable Default Meaning
OUT_DIR dist/ Output directory
MIN_FROM_VERSION 1.0 Oldest version allowed to apply the package
WHEEL_PYTHON_VERSION 3.11 Interpreter the wheels are resolved for
WHEEL_PLATFORMS manylinux_2_28_x86_64 manylinux2014_x86_64 Wheel platforms
APP_TARBALL, COMMIT — Use a prepared payload instead of git archive HEAD

The build uses git archive HEAD, so only committed code is packaged. For unattended signing use --passphrase-file, never --passphrase (arguments are visible in the process table).

Troubleshooting#

"Upload rejected: …"#

The file name does not match the package pattern, the file is empty or larger than 400 MB. Rename or re-download the package and upload again.

"Refused: this package still fails preflight (…)"#

The names in brackets are the blocking checks. Most common: trust (install the release public key with satom execute trust add-key), python (a package built for another interpreter), disk.

Package signed by a key this node does not trust#

Install the public key that signed it on this node (and on the peer), after comparing its fingerprint with the published one.

Apply queued but nothing happens#

satom-updater.path is not enabled on this node. Check with satom get timer status; enable with sudo satom execute enable updater.

Advanced Why the runner is a root-owned copy

satom-updater.service runs as root. Its shipped unit points into /opt/satom, which the service account owns, so deploy/install-runner.sh installs the runner and its verifier as a root:root copy in /usr/local/lib/satom-runner/, run by a system Python and redirected with a drop-in. The package apply refuses to run when the runner is not hardened. The verifier is standard-library only, so it works on a node whose venv is broken.
